Definition: Does the government maintain a digital address register?
Comments: No credible evidence found for digital address register after thorough search; postal codes exist but no national register.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. La Poste Tunisienne operates only a locality-level four-digit postal code system (in place since 1980), and the Office de la Topographie et du Cadastre's "Géoportail cadastral" is a land/parcel cadastre, not a standardised street/building address register. No evidence of a systematic national address database (street names, building numbers) was found in any authoritative source. Value Code 1 (No) confirmed for the correct reason; original comment's underlying conclusion was right despite lacking a citation.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: Linked to national ID/CIN required for voter registration.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Tunisia's Electoral Law (Art. 3 and 6) establishes that voters use their Carte d'Identité Nationale (CIN) and that municipal voter lists are drawn "à partir de la base de données nationale des cartes d'identité nationale". ISIE registration decisions (2014-7, 2017-6) confirm CIN number is entered and checked against the national ID database at registration, but enrolment remains a separate, largely manual/voluntary process (2024/25) rather than a fully automated bidirectional link — so "Partially integrated" (4) rather than "Fully integrated" (5) is the better fit. Value Code 4 confirmed.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: No credible evidence found after searching population register, national population register digital, civil register of persons, INS, Ministry of Interior, World Bank ID4D, UN CRVS reports, e-government portals. Civil status (Madania) serves as foundational system but not a dynamic population register.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Score changed. The original "no evidence" conclusion is contradicted by clear evidence: Décret-loi n°2020-17 (12 May 2020) and Décret n°2020-312 established the Registre de l'Identifiant Unique du Citoyen (RIUC), a continuously-updated, lifetime, backend population register combining civil-register and CIN data with a unique 11-digit identifier for every Tunisian from birth to death. The World Bank's 2020 ID4D diagnostic reports the register already held ~15 million records and was "opérationnel" (register live) while the wider interoperability system was still being built; the ID4Africa 2024 presentation confirms continued rollout (Mobile ID service since August 2022) and further digitisation reforms are underway through 2025-2026. This meets the definition of a population register more closely than a paper civil status system. Recalculated to 4 (Partially deployed) — register operational and populated, but full nationwide interoperability/usage across all agencies still under development. Flagged for human review given the definitional overlap between RIUC (an identifier registry) and a classic "population register"; a reviewer may wish to confirm whether 3 (Under development) is more appropriate if RIUC's live-use status is judged still preliminary.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the business register?
Comments: Business registration generates TIN via RNE-DGI integration.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Business incorporation in Tunisia already requires a declaration d'existence and tax identification (matricule fiscal) from the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) before registration at the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) (Tunisia Investment Authority company-formation guide). As of February 2026, RNE and DGI announced a fully automated single-window platform (arrêté of 12 February 2026) whereby the TIN is generated by DGI and transmitted automatically to RNE to finalise legal registration, replacing the prior manual, disjointed process. This is a live reform (rollout described as imminent as of Feb 2026), so integration is best captured as "Partially integrated" (4) rather than "Fully integrated" (5) until the automated linkage is confirmed fully live and stable. Value Code 4 confirmed on stronger, dated evidence.
